newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SOCCER-FIFA TO DECIDE ON ESTONIA FARCE ON NOVEMBER 7.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA TO DECIDE ON ESTONIA FARCE ON NOVEMBER 7.

text.p: FIFA will announce on November 7 what action it plans to take following the farcical World Cup match between Estonia and Scotland which was abandoned after just three seconds on Wednesday.

Estonia failed to appear at the Kadriorg Stadium for the European group four game after FIFA, world soccer's governing body, agreed to Scotland's request to bring forward the kick-off because of insufficient floodlighting.
FIFA's regulations for the World Cup qualifying competition suggest the Scots will be awarded a 3-0 win by default.

But Scotland will have to wait for FIFA's World Cup organising committee to study reports from Yugoslav referee Miroslav Radoman and FIFA match delegate Jean-Marie Gantenbein, as well as considering a protest from the Estonian Football Association about the kick-off switch.

On Tuesday night, FIFA match delegate Jean-Marie Gantenbein ignored pleas from Scotland coach Craig Brown and Scottish F.A. officials that the temporary floodlights at the stadium were inadequate and that the game should be brought forward.
However, following further protests on Wednesday morning, FIFA ordered the start of the game to be rescheduled to 3 p.m. (1300 GMT) instead of 6.45 p.m. (1545 GMT).
Brown said the lighting was the worst he had seen at an international fixture.
FIFA backed the Scots but the Estonian team did not turn out on the pitch at the appointed time.
The referee blew the whistle to start the match and after three seconds halted it.

Estonian F.A. secretary-general Ainar Lettonon said it had been impossible to get their team to the stadium on time from their training camp and arrange security as the Estonians only knew of the decision in the morning.
"Of course, we will acccept any decision made by FIFA but we have to make sure that the rights of every football association are respected," Lettonen added.
Brown wanted the game to start earlier after he found that two temporary floodlight stanchions were at a different height from two permanent stanchions.
The Estonians said it was impossible to rearrange the match as all the tickets had been sold and live television coverage had been arranged.
FIFA said the reports would be presented to the committee by October 20 and that a decision would be made at the committee's November 7 meeting.

FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper hinted strongly that Scotland would be awarded the match, saying: "Our regulations state that if one team does not report for a match, it shall be considered as having lost and the three points shall be awarded to their opponents with a score of 3-0.
"The Estonian F.A. have indicated they had a logistical problem which prevented them getting to the stadium on time for the revised kick-off and that could be taken into account."
Mart Tarmak, vice-president of the Estonian F.A. said Estonia would be prepared to play Scotland twice away rather than concede the points from Wednesday's aborted match
